why: Markdown and MDX frontmatter is parsed by two YAML libraries: `serde-saphyr` in `crates/ruvyxa_bundler/src/content.rs` and the `yaml` package (core schema) in `packages/ruvyxa/runtime/compiler.mjs`. The page a build pre-renders and the page the Node half compiles must see the same object. Each case is the text between the `---` delimiters and either the frontmatter it parses to or `error: true`. Numbers compare by value: Rust emits `1.0` where JavaScript emits `1`, which evaluate to the same number.

cases.name: nested mappings and sequences
cases.yaml:
title: Hello
author:
  name: Ada
tags: [rust, mdx]
empty_map: {}
empty_seq: []

cases.name: YAML 1.1 boolean spellings stay strings
cases.why: The core schema knows only true/false. serde-saphyr reads yes/no/on/off as booleans unless strict_booleans is set.
cases.yaml:
a: yes
b: no
c: on
d: off
e: y
f: n
g: Yes
h: NO

cases.name: core schema booleans in every case
cases.yaml:
a: True
b: FALSE
c: true

cases.name: every null spelling
cases.yaml:
a: ~
b: null
c: Null
d:
e: NULL

cases.name: dates and timestamps stay strings
cases.why: The core schema has no timestamp type, so a date is the text the author wrote.

cases.name: integers in the core schema's spellings
cases.why: Underscored numbers are strings in the core schema; serde-saphyr parses them unless underscored_numbers_as_strings is set. A leading zero is decimal, not octal.

cases.name: the merge key is an ordinary key
cases.why: YAML 1.2 dropped `<<`; the yaml package only merges under YAML 1.1 or with merge: true.

cases.name: block scalars and their chomping
cases.yaml:
text: |
  line one
  line two
folded: >
  a
  b
keep: |+
  k

strip: |-
  s

cases.name: an unknown tag keeps the value
